back: Matter is made of molecules in continuous random motion, with forces between them that depend on their separation.
Solids and liquids: about one molecular diameter apart (similar densities). Gases at room conditions: about ten diameters apart (density about 1/1000).

front: Force and potential energy against separation
back: Repulsive at short range, zero at r₀, attractive beyond; potential energy is a minimum at r₀. F = −dEp/dr.
The most energetic surface molecules escape, so the mean kinetic energy (temperature) of the remaining liquid falls.
Evaporation: surface only, any temperature, cools. Boiling: throughout, fixed temperature for a given pressure.
Random jerky motion of visible particles caused by uneven bombardment by invisible, randomly moving molecules.
Melting and boiling increase molecular potential energy at constant temperature (constant mean kinetic energy).
Regular lattice (metals, salt); disordered fixed positions (glass); long chain molecules (rubber, polythene).
